findings.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11` — `update` renders the serialized object without mutating anything, and the only caller (`admin-embedding.js.es6:6` `saveChanges`) is not wired to any button in `embedding.hbs`. Both are dead code; drop the `PUT` route (`config/routes.rb:139`) and the action, or implement them.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22` — `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore and papers over the real problem: the codebase now creates records as `'embeddable-host'` (controller) while the store hydrates them as `'embeddable_host'` (from the serializer key). Normalize the type name once in the store instead.
`app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14` — all three method definitions just return the default attribute; delete them and keep the `attributes` line.

`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3` — `create_table … force: true` silently drops an existing table; and a `change` migration containing `execute` + `DELETE FROM site_settings` is not reversible. Use `up`/`down` and drop `force: true`.
No FK or index on `embeddable_hosts.category_id`; deleting a category leaves orphan rows whose `category_id` points at nothing (the admin UI then renders an empty badge).
`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-17` — `record_for_host` returns `false` on a bad URI but `nil` on a miss; pick one. The format regex `[a-z]{2,5}` also rejects `localhost` and newer long TLDs.

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47-49` — `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, so a failed delete leaves the row in place with no feedback (the save path does this correctly).

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:36` — when `categoryId` is null the server defaults to uncategorized, but the client sets `category` to `undefined`, so the badge is blank until reload. Use the server's response (`host.category_id`) instead of the local `categoryId`.
Removing the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings is a breaking change for any plugin or API consumer reading them; worth a note in the upgrade/release notes.
`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13` — the test name "raises an error with a missing host" is now stale since nothing sets/unsets a host.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when looking up the old `embed_category` setting. If the query returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` is blank/missing, or it doesn't match any `categories.name`), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `['id']` will raise, causing the migration to fail before the later fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` can run. This is a concrete, verifiable correctness issue in the diff.

Yes. The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` values using raw SQL interpolation (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) instead of creating `EmbeddableHost` records. This bypasses the model’s `before_validation` normalization in `EmbeddableHost` (stripping `http(s)://` and paths) and its format validation. As a result, existing settings like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` can be migrated into the table untrimmed, which will not match later lookups like `record_for_host` (which compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`) and can break host authorization. Additionally, interpolating `h` directly into SQL can cause migration failure (or worse) if it contains quotes.

In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the line `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the SQL query returns at least one row. In Discourse, the `site_settings` table typically only contains overridden settings, so there may be no `embed_category` row at all. If the result set is empty, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` will raise a `NoMethodError`, causing the migration to fail before reaching the later `if category_id == 0` fallback.

In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, the query uses `lower(host) = ?` but binds the raw `host` string without downcasing it. Since `before_validation` strips scheme/path but does not downcase, and the format validation is case-insensitive (`/i`), the DB can contain mixed/uppercase host values. If the input `host` contains uppercase (e.g., from `URI(host).host` or a stored record), `lower(host) = 'Example.COM'` will not match and a valid allowed host could be rejected. The fix would be to compare against `host.downcase` (or normalize `host` to lowercase on save).

In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy` the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy`. If the record doesn’t exist, `host` will be `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` (e.g., `nil.host=` in `save_host` or `nil.destroy` in `destroy`) instead of a proper 404/JSON error response. This is a concrete correctness/robustness bug introduced by the diff at the referenced lines.

In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., params missing/blank in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` where `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`), this will raise `NoMethodError` before validations can add an error. The DB `null: false` constraint doesn't prevent this runtime exception during validation callbacks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11` — `update` renders the serialized object without mutating anything, and the only caller (`admin-embedding.js.es6:6` `saveChanges`) is not wired to any button in `embedding.hbs`. Both are dead code; drop the `PUT` route (`config/routes.rb:139`) and the action, or implement them.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct and does not persist any changes (there are no params read or mutations performed). The corresponding client action `saveChanges` in `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that PUT endpoint, but `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` contains no button or other UI element wired to `saveChanges` (only `addHost` and per-host save/delete actions exist). This makes the PUT route (`put "customize/embedding"`) and `update` action effectively unused and non-functional in the diff as-is, matching the finding's claim of dead/no-op code unless further implementation is added elsewhere (not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22` — `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore and papers over the real problem: the codebase now creates records as `'embeddable-host'` (controller) while the store hydrates them as `'embeddable_host'` (from the serializer key). Normalize the type name once in the store instead.
`app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14` — all three method definitions just return the default attribute; delete them and keep the `attributes` line.

adjudication.rationale: The serializer explicitly declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id`, and the methods `id`, `host`, and `category_id` merely return `object.id`, `object.host`, and `object.category_id`, which is the default behavior for declared attributes in an `ApplicationSerializer`. Removing these methods would be a minor cleanup/refactor, not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3` — `create_table … force: true` silently drops an existing table; and a `change` migration containing `execute` + `DELETE FROM site_settings` is not reversible. Use `up`/`down` and drop `force: true`.

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (potentially deleting data) instead of failing fast. Additionally, the migration is defined with `def change` but performs multiple raw `execute` calls (data copy/INSERTs and `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN (...)`). Rails cannot automatically reverse these operations, so this `change` migration is not reversible in the normal way; it should be written with explicit `up`/`down` (or `reversible`) if reversibility is desired.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No FK or index on `embeddable_hosts.category_id`; deleting a category leaves orphan rows whose `category_id` points at nothing (the admin UI then renders an empty badge).

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts` with a `category_id` column (null: false) but does not add an index or any foreign key constraint. The model `EmbeddableHost` just `belongs_to :category` with no `dependent` handling, and nothing in the diff updates embeddable host rows when a Category is deleted. If a category is deleted, existing `embeddable_hosts.category_id` values can point to a non-existent category; on the client the template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`, and `host.category` can be nil if hydration cannot resolve the deleted category ID, resulting in an empty/missing badge. This is a concrete integrity/correctness gap introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-17` — `record_for_host` returns `false` on a bad URI but `nil` on a miss; pick one. The format regex `[a-z]{2,5}` also rejects `localhost` and newer long TLDs.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `EmbeddableHost` model, `record_for_host` explicitly returns `false` for malformed/blank URIs (`return false unless uri.present?`, etc.) but returns `nil` when the query misses (`where(...).first`). That creates inconsistent return types (record/false/nil) for the same “no record” outcome, which is a real correctness/API contract issue even if current callers happen to tolerate it. Also, the validation regex `\.[a-z]{2,5}` rejects valid hosts with longer modern TLDs (e.g. `.museum`, `.technology`) and any host without a dot (e.g. `localhost`), which would prevent configuring legitimate embeddable hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47-49` — `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, so a failed delete leaves the row in place with no feedback (the save path does this correctly).

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); }); but does not attach a .catch(popupAjaxError) (unlike save(), which does). If destroyRecord() fails (network/server error), no error is surfaced and the UI provides no feedback; the row will also not be removed because sendAction is only in the success handler, leaving the user without explanation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:36` — when `categoryId` is null the server defaults to uncategorized, but the client sets `category` to `undefined`, so the badge is blank until reload. Use the server's response (`host.category_id`) instead of the local `categoryId`.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `embeddable-host.js.es6` save action, `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` may be `null` (new host defaults `categoryId: null`, and `cantSave` doesn’t require a category). Server-side `save_host` then defaults blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. However, after `host.save(props)` resolves, the client does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`; when `categoryId` is `null`, `findById(null)` yields `undefined`, so `host.category` becomes `undefined` and the `{{category-badge host.category}}` renders blank until reload/rehydration. The fix is to use the saved record’s `category_id` (from the response) or avoid overwriting `category` when `categoryId` is blank.

In the diff, `config/locales/client.en.yml` adds `admin.embedding.edit: "edit"`, but none of the added templates/components reference that key. The UI uses only `admin.embedding.title`, `confirm_delete`, `host`, `category`, and `add_host`; the edit button is icon-only (`{{d-button icon="pencil" ...}}`) with no label/i18n lookup. So the key appears unused, but this is just a dead/unused translation string and does not introduce a functional bug or correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings is a breaking change for any plugin or API consumer reading them; worth a note in the upgrade/release notes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` settings from `config/site_settings.yml`, deletes their server-side i18n entries, removes `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`, and includes a migration that deletes those site_settings rows (`DELETE ... IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`). Any plugin/custom code/API consumer that still reads `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` or `SiteSetting.embed_category` (or calls the removed helper) would break after upgrade, so noting this as a breaking change in upgrade/release notes is justified by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13` — the test name "raises an error with a missing host" is now stale since nothing sets/unsets a host.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated spec, the test "raises an error with a missing host" no longer sets `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil` because the implementation moved from a site setting to the `EmbeddableHost` table. The test still triggers an error by *not* fabricating any `EmbeddableHost` record (and also not stubbing a referer), which makes `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` return false and the controller respond with an error. So while the wording of the test name may be slightly imprecise, it is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff (the test is still meaningfully testing the “no allowed host configured / not allowed” case).
